mesoscaleDiscussions.summary: Thunderstorm development is anticipated across far southwest Oklahoma and into the Texas Panhandle/northwest Texas by late afternoon. This activity will pose a threat for severe downburst winds as it spreads southwest through early evening. Watch issuance is possible

details.label: Summary
details.text: Thunderstorm development is anticipated across far southwest Oklahoma and into the Texas Panhandle/northwest Texas by late afternoon. This activity will pose a threat for severe downburst winds as it spreads southwest through early evening. Watch issuance is possible

details.label: Discussion
details.text: Recent surface observations are reporting temperatures reaching into the 106-110 F range within the apex of a thermal ridge across northwest TX. These temperatures are running 4-5 F warmer than expected based on the latest high-res guidance, which implies that boundary-layer mixing is likely deeper than depicted by forecast soundings. Similarly, residual mixed-layer inhibition is likely weaker than recent RAP mesoanalyses would suggest. The early stages of boundary-layer cumulus development are becoming evident in GOES imagery, suggesting that thunderstorm development appears probable in the coming hours either along a residual outflow boundary draped across southwest OK, along a diffuse/weak frontal zone extending into the TX Panhandle, or in proximity to a weak thermal low analyzed near the intersection of these two boundaries. Although recent guidance does not appear to be capturing low-level thermodynamic conditions well, HRRR/RRFS time-lagged guidance shows a trends towards widely scattered to scattered thunderstorm development by the 20-22 UTC period. Deep-layer shear will remain weak and promote mainly disorganized convection, but the potential for severe downbursts should increase as thunderstorms spread south/southwest into the thermal ridge where low-level profiles will be most optimal for near-surface downdraft accelerations. Explicit wind gusts estimates from high-res solutions depict small swaths of 60-75 mph winds, which appear reasonable given the expectation of poorly organized convection within a very hot/deeply mixed environment. Convective trends will continue to be monitored, and watch issuance is possible if convective coverage appears sufficient for a more widespread severe wind threat

details.label: Summary
details.text: The threat for isolated occurrences of large hail and severe wind gusts is expected to increase by mid-afternoon and continue through this evening. A watch is currently not anticipated due to the limited coverage of the threat

details.label: Discussion
details.text: Recent trends in visible satellite imagery show deepening moist convection along the Laramie Mountains and CO Front Range with additional development likely ahead of a well-defined MCV moving through central WY. Beneath a plume of steep mid-level lapse rates, current surface observations indicate a moist boundary layer characterized by dewpoints in the mid 50s to low 60s, yielding MLCAPE of 1000-1500 J/kg. Latest objective analysis suggests the air mass across the adjacent High Plains remains capped; however, continued daytime heating and the glancing influence of the WY MCV should allow initial terrain-anchored storms to move into lower elevations later this afternoon into evening. Current VWPs and RAP-based forecast soundings indicate vertically veering wind profiles with around 30 kt of deep-layer shear, which will be supportive of at least episodic supercell structures capable of large hail. The potential for isolated severe wind gusts may become more likely by early evening, especially if storms can merge into clusters

details.text: Isolated severe storms appear possible from mid-afternoon into this evening. Damaging wind gusts are the primary hazard. A watch issuance is not anticipated due to the limited areal coverage of the threat

details.label: Discussion
details.text: Recent thunderstorm development has occurred over the WV Panhandle, northwest of Harrisonburg, VA, amidst a moist and moderately unstable air mass with MLCAPE of 1500-2000 J/kg. Farther east along the lee side of the Blue Ridge, visible satellite imagery indicates deepening cumulus within a low-level upslope regime. Latest time-lagged HRRR and RRFS ensemble guidance suggests that a small cluster of thunderstorms may evolve out of those areas of deepening moist convection over northern VA later this afternoon into evening. The current VWP from Charleston, WV is sampling 30-40 kt of westerly winds above 4 km AGL, which may contribute to some organization as updrafts continue to mature this afternoon. When coupled with steepening low-level lapse rates, the environment appears supportive of locally damaging wind gusts as storms progress east across the discussion area

details.label: Summary
details.text: Scattered damaging/severe wind gusts and isolated large hail are expected across portions of the Mid South this afternoon. A Severe Thunderstorm Watch will likely be needed

details.label: Discussion
details.text: Latest surface analysis depicts a west-east oriented cold front extending from far southern Illinois into southern Missouri and Kansas. Also evident in visible satellite imagery are an MCV located in close proximity to ongoing convection across far southeastern Kansas and a surface confluence zone across northern Arkansas demarcated by a zone of developing cumulus. As this MCV and surface cold front continue to progress south-southeastward through mid-afternoon, guidance suggests that ongoing convection should intensify and/or additional development will occur along the aforementioned boundaries amid a moderately unstable environment. As convective coverage increases through the mid-afternoon, enhanced mid-level flow associated with the MCV (40-50 kts sampled by the Tulsa/Wichita VWPs along the southern flank of the MCV) will aid in the organization of convection into one or more linear clusters. Scattered damaging/severe wind gusts (and potentially a few significant gusts to 75-80 mph) are likely to accompany this cluster given the enhanced mid-level flow and presence of very steep low-to-mid level lapse rates below 600 mb (as depicted by recent objective analysis and sampled by the 12 UTC LZK observed sounding). A Severe Thunderstorm Watch will likely be needed in the next 1-2 hours to address this severe risk
